title: The Love Story of the Taj Mahal
paragraphs: The Taj Mahal in Agra, India, is one of the most famous buildings in the world. Every year, it attracts huge numbers of visitors. But it is not a palace. It is a tomb, and it was built because of a love story.

In the early 1600s, a young prince named Khurram met a girl named Arjumand Banu Begum. The two were engaged in 1607 and married in 1612. After the wedding, she was given the name Mumtaz Mahal, which means "chosen one of the palace." The prince later became emperor of the Mughal Empire and took the name Shah Jahan.

Mumtaz Mahal traveled with her husband, even on military campaigns, and she was also his trusted adviser. The couple had 14 children, but only seven survived past infancy. In 1631, Mumtaz Mahal died while giving birth to their 14th child.

Shah Jahan was heartbroken. He decided to build a beautiful tomb for his wife. Work on the Taj Mahal began around 1632, and the whole complex was finished in 1653. According to a French traveler of the time, more than 20,000 workers and 1,000 elephants were used. The building is made of white marble, and its walls are decorated with precious stones.
The story of Shah Jahan has a sad ending. In 1658, his son Aurangzeb took power and kept him locked up in Agra Fort. Shah Jahan died in 1666, and he was buried next to his wife inside the Taj Mahal.
In 1983, the Taj Mahal became a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Today, it is still seen as a symbol of love.
